title: spec/appendix-ccp12-hopping.md: Python implementation uses different minimum divisor than spec
description:
Line 84 specifies N = MAX(NChannels - 1, 2) but the Python implementation at line 305 uses n = max(n_channels - 1, 1). When NChannels = 2: spec gives N=2 (channels 1-2 possible), but Python gives n=1 (always channel 1). This inconsistency causes different channel selection behavior.

Fix suggestion: Align the Python implementation with the spec by changing 'max(n_channels - 1, 1)' to 'max(n_channels - 1, 2)', or update the spec if the Python behavior is intended.
close_reason: Invalid: The bead description is inaccurate. The spec (line 85) correctly states MAX(NChannels-1,2) and the Python implementations match this. The 'line 305' reference points to the spec's example code which also uses max(n_channels-1,2), not 1. The actual Python implementations in ccp.py:97 and channel_plan.py use max(...,2). link/channel.py handles edge cases explicitly (n_channels<=2 returns constant), which is CORRECT behavior since the spec's formula would return out-of-bounds channel 2 when only 2 channels exist. Note: tdma.py has a DIFFERENT bug (uses max(num_channels,3)) - file separately if needed.
